review_cost.rationale: Approve after nits: a round of questions about the filter-input approach and the redundant catch-all route, plus removal of the unused dependency. Nothing requires structural rework.

findings.issue: Filter state is managed with uncontrolled inputs, three refs, a debounce ref and two DOM-mutating sync effects, navigating manually — a home-grown version of what React Router provides via <Form method="get">/useSubmit/useSearchParams.
findings.suggestion: Use controlled inputs bound to useSearchParams (or a GET <Form> with debounced submit for the search box) so URL, DOM and React state can't drift; keep the pre-hydration reconciliation only if tests demand it.

findings.issue: Splat route whose loader throws 404 while the component renders null; React Router already renders the root ErrorBoundary with a 404 for unmatched URLs, so this adds indirection without changing behavior.
findings.suggestion: Drop the splat route and let the framework's unmatched-URL 404 hit the root ErrorBoundary, or render the Not found UI directly in this route module instead of returning null.

findings.issue: Card sprite URLs are constructed from the /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png pattern rather than taken from the API's front_default, coupling the app to the media layout.
findings.suggestion: Use the sprite URL the API returns (falling back to the pattern only if null) so the app can't desync from the data.

findings.issue: Errors are only console.error'd in development, so production loader failures are silently swallowed with no log or report hook.
findings.suggestion: Log unconditionally in production (RR's error-reporting guide suggests a handleError export on the root) even though the UI stays generic.

findings.issue: isbot is declared as a dependency but never imported; the framework's default server entry owns bot detection now.
The Move wire-type is defined independently in routes/pokemon.tsx and routes/move.tsx, so a shape change must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Move the shared Move (and NamedResource/Translated-based) shapes into lib/types.ts.

findings.issue: The cache Map never evicts expired entries; they're only replaced on next access and rejection. Bounded in practice by the API's URL space, but it's implicit global state relying on that assumption.
findings.suggestion: Delete expired entries on read (a cheap one-liner) and note the bounded-by-URL-space assumption in the comment.

findings.issue: Every Pokémon page load fetches the version-group list and all ~35 version-group records (each individually cached), so cold-start does a large parallel fan-out per unique URL.
findings.suggestion: Cache the assembled name→order map under a single key with the same cached() helper so the first hit per TTL costs one composite entry, or reuse the index.

findings.issue: columns.find(...) with a non-null assertion; safe today because sort keys come from rendered columns, but brittle if the column set ever changes dynamically.
findings.suggestion: Derive the sort column once at toggle time or guard the null case.

summary: This is a confident, current-idiom React Router v8 app: typed route modules, the Layout root convention, data() 404s, React 19 <title> elements (which v8 now recommends over meta), a clean .server.ts data boundary, and a correct minimal express server. The main thing a reviewer would push on is the home page's uncontrolled-ref filter plumbing where Form/useSubmit/useSearchParams would do the job, plus a redundant catch-all route, an unused isbot dependency, and a couple of minor fragilities (constructed sprite URLs, DEV-only error logging). Mergeable after one light round of comments.
